desc: A proud-looking tiefling rises from a bow, facing his rival with a smirk. As soon as their rapiers are drawn, he rushes forward, gracefully blocking their potentially fatal hit and piercing through them in the same breath.

A human woman blocks a wyverns claws with her sword, gritting her teeth and digging her heels into the ground. As it snaps at her, she quickly slams her sword into its jaw, both deflecting its attack and slicing through its face, and it collapses. She neglects her wounds to wave at her audience, a large grin across her face as they cheer and the dust settles.

intro.name: Master Duelists
desc: Not every swordsman is a blade savant—while other people may focus on being a jack of all trades, blade savants generally stick to a few specific techniques and hone them to perfection. One of their main focuses is remaining light-footed and using their own weapon as a shield.

Blade savants easily parry their opponents attacks, turning what would surely skewer another person into merely a scratch. This, combined with the way that they seem to predict their opponents moves, makes for a frightening defense.

intro.name: Returning the Favor
desc: The amount of warriors who have ended up on the receiving end of a blade savants weapon all seem to have the same thing to say: whatever you do to them, they seem to take it almost personally, and sharpen their blade to do thrice back to their attackers. Some people like to extend this into calling them arrogant, thin-skinned—but this isn’t quite correct.

More experienced savants have learned to turn the adrenaline from near-hits into an almost uncanny focus. These close calls fuel them and push them to do better, feeding into the initial urge that pushed them down this path. And if a few of them do happen to align with that assessment, that trait only makes them go above and beyond.

intro.name: Creating a Blade Savant
desc: While creating a blade savant, you should think about what led to their training--both with the sword and with tactics--as well as their confidence. Were you a noble who hired an elite mentor? Or are you self-taught, making your own techniques and observing others from afar? How did you learn to think a step ahead of your enemies on the battlefield?

Why have you set out on an adventure? Do you simply wish to become a blade of legend, or are you motivated by something else? When did you first pick up your weapon? It may have been a sword passed down to you by your parents or a mentor, one you happened on by chance, or one you got from becoming a soldier.

Before joining this adventure, how did you live? You could’ve been a tactician in the military, a pit fighter, or perhaps you have only just found your confidence and are only just starting to set out into the world. No matter your background, your sword is one of your most important possessions, functioning as both your offense and defense.

intro.name: Quick Build
desc: You can make a Blade Savant quickly by following these suggestions. First, make Dexterity your highest ability score, or Strength if you are going to choose the Doppelsöldner blade technique. Your next-highest score should be Intelligence, followed by Constitution. Second, choose the Noble or Folk Hero background.

class-features.name: Class Features
desc: As a Blade Savant you gain the following class features.

list.Skills:: Choose three from the following: Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Insight, Investigation, Perception, and Performance.

class-features.name: Equipment
desc: You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

list.a: (a) a rapier, (b) a shortsword, or (c) a scimitar
list.b: (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) two daggers
list.c: (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

class-features.name: Parry and Riposte
desc: You have learned how to redirect your opponents blows and then use that opening to retaliate. When you are hit by a weapon attack you can use your reaction to spend a Parry die and reduce the damage by 1d4 + your Dexterity modifier. Additionally, you can make a melee weapon attack against the attacker as part of the same reaction, referred to as a riposte.

You have an amount of Parry dice equal to half your Blade Savant level (rounded up) + your Intelligence modifier and regain all dice during a short or long rest. You must be wielding a melee weapon that has the finesse property or deals slashing damage to use this feature.
Your Parry die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d6 at 3rd level, a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 9th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

class-features.name: Unarmored Defense
desc: You are able to see through any feint attack and predict where your opponent is going to attack from next. Starting from 1st level, if you are wearing no armor and are not wielding a shield, your armor class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Intelligence modifier.

class-features.name: Retribution
desc: Starting at 2nd level, when you spend a Parry die you then gain a Retribution die. After an hour out of combat, you lose all Retribution dice. The size of your Retribution dice is the same as your Parry die.
When you parry or roll for weapon damage, you can use an amount of Retribution dice up to your Proficiency Bonus to add to the roll.

class-features.name: Duelist's Insight
desc: At 2nd level, you notice particular things about another person’s capabilities. When you use your Parry and Riposte feature against another creature, you learn one of the following characteristics of your choice:

list.a: One of their weapon or armor proficiencies
list.b: One of their saving throw proficiencies

descfoot: Alternatively, you learn a characteristic of the DM's choice.
You can only use this feature once per minute.

class-features.name: Blade Technique
desc: At 3rd level, you choose to specialize in a specific technique. Choose Sabreur, Doppelsöldner, or Battōka, all detailed at the end of the class description. The technique you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

class-features.name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

class-features.name: Extra Attack
desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

class-features.name: Evasion
desc: At 7th level, your ability to predict your enemy’s actions lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon’s lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

class-features.name: Sharp-Witted
desc: Beginning at 13th level, your analytical prowess extends beyond combat. You can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Wisdom, for Perception and Insight skill checks.
Additionally, you gain a +5 to your passive Perception, Insight and Investigation scores.

class-features.name: Unyielding
desc: At 14th level, your confidence and sense of self has been fully honed and your focus cannot be swayed. You are immune to the charmed and frightened conditions.

class-features.name: Full Counter
desc: Starting at 18th level, after you successfully reduce damage from a weapon attack to 0 using your Parry and Riposte feature, you regain your Reaction. You may use Retribution dice to achieve this.

class-features.name: Invulnerable Focus
desc: At 20th level, your speed and cunning in combat is unparalleled. When you roll initiative and have no parries left, you regain half of your total parries, rounded down.

subclasses.name: Blade Techniques
desc: Like other classes, blade savants choose an archetype by third level. These archetypes are mostly based on different types of real combat styles, ranging from the fencers of France to the knife-throwers of Central Africa.

subclasses.name: Sabreur
desc: Masters at one-on-ones, sabreurs are known for their impressive duels and ability to pick out their opponents weaknesses. Their choice to excel in this field makes them quite feared in the high society of countries that still settle feuds via duel—after all, what argument is worth your potential death, or worse, loss of face?

subclasses.name: En Garde
desc: Starting at 3rd level, you may use your bonus action to mark one creature as your opponent for 1 minute. The mark ends early if you fall unconscious, you die, or if combat ends. While the creature is marked, you gain the following benefits:

list.a: You roll an additional amount of damage dice equal to half your proficiency bonus rounded down when determining riposte damage against your chosen opponent.
list.b: Any attack roll against your chosen opponent is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

descfoot: You can use this feature up to 2 times, and you regain all uses during a long rest.

subclasses.name: Advance
desc: At 6th level, when you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to 15 feet towards it after it has finished moving. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

subclasses.name: Engage
desc: Beginning at 11th level, when you first mark a creature using your En Garde feature, you can choose to make them make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. On a failed save, the marked creature cannot use its action for anything other than attacking you. At the end of each of its turns, it can make another Intelligence saving throw. On a success, this effect ends.

subclasses.name: Remise
desc: At 17th level, you learn to pinpoint your opponents vitals to cause massive damage. Whenever you score a critical hit with a one-handed piercing weapon, the target suffers an additional amount of damage equal to half the damage dealt at the end of its next turn.

subclasses.name: Doppelsöldner
desc: Doppelsöldner are impressive front liners--first to charge in, yet often the last ones standing. While many in forlorn hope ranks fall, some of them rise above the rest and spend years rushing forward and carving a path for their comrades. And after the fight is done? They relish the additional pay they receive for their courage.

subclasses.name: Hold the Line
desc: Starting from 3rd level, you can choose to use your Strength modifier, instead of your Dexterity modifier, to your Unarmored Defense and Parry and Riposte damage reduction. Additionally, your maximum hit points increase by 3 hit points, and each time you gain a level in this class you gain one additional hit point.

subclasses.name: Breakthrough
desc: At 3rd level, you know exactly how to rush down your enemies. You can stow and draw weapons as a free action. When you make a ranged weapon attack on your turn, you can then use your bonus action to move up to your speed towards your target.

If you move up to your full speed or end your movement within ten feet of the target, the next time you use your Parry and Riposte feature before your next turn you additionally gain resistance to the attack that triggered it.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier and regain all uses during a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Lock Horns
desc: Starting from 6th level, after rolling initiative but before anyone has taken their turn, you can make one ranged attack. When you attack in this way, you can then use your Breakthrough feature as a free action and without expending any usages.
Additionally, you have resistance to all damage during the first round of combat.

subclasses.name: Run Them Down
desc: At 11th level, when you use your Breakthrough feature and end within ten feet of the original target, the next time you attack them before your next turn and spend Retribution dice to add to the damage roll, you double the chosen amount without expending any additional dice.

subclasses.name: Mettle
desc: Starting at 17th level, even in times of desperation you know you will make it through. If you have no more than half your hit points (rounded up) left, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subclasses.name: Battōka
desc: The quickest draw, battōka are masters of deflecting their opponents blows and weaving through the battlefield. They pride themselves on their incredible reflexes, and catching one off-guard is nigh-impossible. Even when surrounded by enemies or facing a particularly nimble opponent, a battōka never lets them off without a response.

subclasses.name: Swift Counter
desc: Beginning at 3rd level, you can fend off your opponents with truly unrivaled speed. If you are attacked a second time after using your Parry and Riposte feature before the start of your next turn, you can Parry and Riposte the attack without using your reaction, spending the Parry die as you would normally.

subclasses.name: Refocus
desc: Starting at 6th level, you can use a bonus action to regain an amount of Parry dice equal to your Intelligence modifier.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

subclasses.name: Slipstream
desc: Starting at 11th level, your parries can unsteady your opponents guard. When you use your Parry and Riposte feature, you can choose to move up to 10 feet away as part of the same reaction without provoking opportunity attacks.

subclasses.name: Whirlwind Guard
desc: Starting at 17th level, you can use your Action to assume a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in this stance, you have unlimited reactions. You can only use your reaction to use the Parry and Riposte feature or to make an opportunity attack.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again.

subclasses.name: Spellward
desc: A unique and somewhat rare breed, spellwards are savants that focus on overtaking mages by using their own magic against them. This focus on mages sometimes earns them the title of witch hunters in magic circles, or outright bans of the practice in certain countries. However, this fear isn’t unfounded—they have been an effective tool in particularly mage-despising tyrants pockets in the past.

They aren’t known for just this, of course—while their reputation may vary from place to place, they are also known for their ability and bond with their weapons. They often create their own just so that they can have the perfect match, and since they themselves do not typically have an inherent ability to counter mages, this is their most important tool.

subclasses.name: Inscribed Blade
desc: Starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in Smith’s Tools. Additionally, over the course of a long rest, you can modify an existing blade (magical or nonmagical) into an inscribed blade.

list.a: This weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
list.b: You can only have one inscribed blade at a time. If you create a new inscribed blade, the previous one loses any abilities associated with this feature, and is no longer considered an inscribed blade.

subclasses.name: Absorption
desc: Also at 3rd level, you can use your Parry and Riposte feature against damaging spell attacks if you are wielding your inscribed blade.
When used in this way, your blade absorbs the damage type of the spell. You can only have one damage type absorbed at any time, and if you absorb a new damage type, the previous is lost.
The next time you expend Retribution dice on a weapon damage roll after using this feature, you can choose to make the extra damage that of the absorbed damage type. You then lose the absorbed type.

subclasses.name: Dispeller
desc: At 6th level, once per 10 minutes you can use your sword to point out the nearest magical source within 30 feet and determine its school of magic.
Additionally, you can use your sword to cast Dispel Magic or Remove Curse once per day.

subclasses.name: Soul Draw
desc: At 11th level, when you reduce a creature with the Spellcasting feature to 0 points, you gain Retribution dice equal to the level of their highest spell (up to your proficiency modifier). The damage type absorbed from doing so is force damage.

subclasses.name: Spellstealer
desc: At 17th level, when you see a creature within 5 feet casting a spell, you can use your Reaction to make a melee weapon attack. If this attack hits, you can force them to make a Constitution save. The DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

On a failed save, the spell fails and has no effect. Additionally, if you’re wielding your inscribed blade, you absorb the spell and gain an amount of Retribution dice equal to the spell’s level. The damage type absorbed from doing this is force damage. On a successful save, nothing happens.
You can use this feature an amount of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), and regain all uses during a short or long rest.

multiclass.name: Multiclassing
desc: If your group uses the multiclassing rules from the Player’s Handbook, here’s what you need to know if you choose blade savant as one of your classes.
Prerequisites. To qualify for multiclassing into Blade Savant, you must meet these prerequisites: Dexterity and Intelligence of 13 or higher.
Proficiencies. When you multiclass into the Blade Savant class, you gain the following proficiencies: Light armor, simple weapons, martial weapons.

feats.name: Blade Savant Initiate
desc: You’ve trained extensively with blades, allowing your reflexes to become exceptionally good. You gain the following benefits:

list.a: You gain three parry dice. If you already have parry dice, they are of the same size as your current parry dice. Otherwise, they are d6s.
list.b: When you are hit by a weapon attack, you can expend a parry die to reduce the damage by your parry die size + your Dexterity modifier. Additionally, you can make a melee weapon attack against the attacker as part of the same reaction, referred to as a riposte. You must be wielding a melee weapon that has the finesse property or deals slashing damage to use this feature.
list.c: You regain all expended parry dice when you finish a short or long rest.
